confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from crowdsourced cost-of-living aggregators found in a web search (Nomad Watch, Expatistan, livingcost/citycost-type comparisons). These sources give an inexpensive meal at about USD 6.70–8.00, mid-range dinner for two at about USD 54, cappuccino at about USD 2.80–3.25 and beer at about CLP 2,830–3,900 per pint. They use different dates and definitions, so some uncertainty remains. I did not search directly for cocktail and wine prices. I estimated them from the local relationship to beer prices and from typical Chilean pisco sour and house wine pricing, so they are less certain. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates based on general knowledge of Arica's modest backpacker scene and mid-range hotel market, not on any listing inspection.
comparable_city_reasoning: Arica is a mid-sized northern Chilean beach and border city. Its prices are somewhat below Santiago and roughly similar to Iquique and La Serena. Hostel supply is limited and is aimed at surfers and overland travellers coming from Peru and Bolivia.
